To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and compared simple, rapid and reproducible protocols based on membrane filtrations and/or solid phase extractions, allowing the recovery of low molecular weight fraction in rat plasma.
we developed a simple and robust fractionation protocol that allows for the detection of low abundance plasma peptides, including fibrinopeptides, in the femtomolar range.
we developed and compared different protocols for fractionation of low molecular weight fraction from rat plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of low abundant plasma peptides by mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
the identification of low molecular weight plasma biomarkers.
the development of new analytical methods and the use of new analytical techniques for the analysis of peptides and proteins in complex biological samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of the fractionation protocols presented here, with the nanoLC-Chip-MS/MS analysis, would allow identification of peptides in rat plasma representing ~10−7% of total proteins.

the combination of membrane filtration and SPE, in the case of the plasma sample, is the most effective and reproducible approach to obtain the low molecular weight plasma fraction, and that the use of MALDI-TOFIQ/TOF-MS for peptide quantitation, in the case that no standard is available for the target peptide, is a very effective and reliable strategy.
the protocol presented here allows the detection and identification of low abundance and/or small peptides in rat plasma, with a sensitivity in the femtomolar range.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed and validated an efficient protocol for the detection and identification of low molecular weight endogenous peptides from the plasma of rats.

a combination of membrane filtration, solid-phase extraction, reverse phase HPLChromatography and MALDI-TOFSpectroscopy allows detection, in a highly reproducible manner, of more than 300 low molecular weight plasma peptides, with an LOD of 1fmol/μL.
we developed and validated a new method to enrich the low-molecular-weight fraction of plasma, which allows the detection and identification of low abundance peptides in a reproducible way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a membrane filtration step with a solid phase extraction step is the best strategy to enrich low molecular weight plasma peptides.
it is possible to enrich for the low molecular weight peptides in plasma by a combination of membrane filtration, solid-phase extraction, and reverse phase HPLCh.

it is possible to detect and characterize endogenous peptides in plasma, using mass spectrometry, and that the fractionation strategy we developed can be used to enrich for low abundance peptides in plasma.
